html:
The Israel-Jordan peace treaty was signed on 26 October 1994 at the Arava border crossing, north of Aqaba and Eilat, by the prime ministers of the two countries, with King Hussein and Israel's Yitzhak Rabin present.

Jordan was the second Arab state to make peace with Israel, after Egypt in 1979. The treaty fixed the border, shared out water from the Jordan and Yarmuk rivers, and recognised Jordan's special role at the Muslim holy places of Jerusalem. It followed the Oslo Accords of 1993.

The peace has held, with security and gas deals, though it remains unpopular with many Jordanians. See also Jordan.
